slot_m1_layer0_ambient_carrier.carrier: Alphabet, AlphabetBijection, AtomSet, DiscreteCategory, FreeMonoid, IsoSet
slot_m1_layer0_ambient_carrier.original_target: Free monoids on finite alphabets of different sizes are not isomorphic; discrete categories with different finite object counts are not equivalent. So a numeral/alphabet re-presentation cannot be an isomorphism of structure.
slot_m1_layer0_ambient_carrier.source_scope_review: The sources are general: Paper.lean and Paper001.lean prove, over List A and List alpha with hand-rolled structures, that an isomorphism induces an alphabet bijection (Classical.choice is used for it, per Paper.lean header) and hence equal sizes. Paper001.lean DiscreteEquiv is, by definition, a pair of mutually inverse maps on objects, so no_discrete_equivalence is the pigeonhole fact; the Python checks free_monoids_nonisomorphic and discrete_categories_inequivalent compare counts (the latter returns left != right). The DAG-local Lean theorem pg_to_sn_and_wdp_route_chain_composition is fixed arithmetic and vacuous for this node. This node re-proves the statement with Mathlib FreeMonoid / MulEquiv and Discrete categories (genuine categorical equivalence), bridges the source WordIso to MulEquiv, adds the converse iff, and records the sharp boundary: a set bijection exists, so the obstruction is multiplicativity; native: exact word counts, brute-force atoms, exhaustive homomorphism search with bounded image length, discrete equivalences, shortlex bijection.

claim_boundary.supports: For arbitrary alphabets (kernel-checked, lean4/FreeMonoidNoniso.lean, Mathlib FreeMonoid and CategoryTheory.Discrete): a monoid isomorphism FreeMonoid a ~ FreeMonoid b induces a bijection of the alphabets (the atoms are the one-letter words and an isomorphism permutes atoms), so unequal finite alphabets give non-isomorphic free monoids, and FreeMonoid a ~ FreeMonoid b iff a ~ b; alphabetEquiv, no_free_monoid_iso, freeMonoid_iso_iff_equiv, set_bijection_exists and the discrete-category theorems use Classical.choice (kernel axiom reports: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), as does the source for the same step; an equivalence of discrete categories Discrete a ~ Discrete b (a genuine CategoryTheory.Equivalence) gives a bijection a ~ b, so Fin n and Fin m give equivalent discrete categories iff n = m; every source WordIso yields a MulEquiv (WordIso.toMulEquiv) and the source theorem is recovered through it; the converse MulEquiv -> WordIso is not stated; the boundary is sharp: for n, m >= 1 the underlying SETS of FreeMonoid (Fin n) and FreeMonoid (Fin m) are in bijection (both countably infinite), so the content is multiplicativity, not cardinality; the free monoid on the empty alphabet is one point; words of length k over Fin n number n^k and atoms number n. Exhaustive native checks on 15 alphabet pairs (sizes 0 to 4): all homomorphisms whose generator images have length <= 1 for the pairs (3,4), (4,3), (4,4) and length <= 2 for all other pairs; the candidates injective on words of length <= 2 whose images contain every letter (a necessary-condition filter, not a proof of bijectivity) are exactly the n! letter permutations when n = m and none otherwise; the equivalences of discrete categories are exactly the bijections; and the explicit shortlex bijection of the underlying sets is multiplicative on the first 30 words exactly when n = m (a prefix statement).
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Any structure on numerals or alphabets other than the free-monoid multiplication or the discrete category (a numeral or alphabet re-presentation may still be a non-isomorphic map, a set bijection, or an isomorphism of some other structure; no other structure, such as free commutative monoids, is examined); language restriction, partial recovery and total erasure (separate ledger row WDP-P001-009); infinite alphabets beyond the general Lean statement; the native homomorphism search covers short generator images only and is an instance, not the general theorem.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: A monoid isomorphism between free monoids on any two alphabets induces a bijection of the alphabets, so free monoids on finite alphabets of different sizes are not isomorphic and discrete categories with different finite object counts are not equivalent; a bare bijection of the underlying sets does exist for sizes at least one, so a numeral or alphabet re-presentation cannot be an isomorphism of the free-monoid (word concatenation) structure or of the discrete-category structure; other structures are not addressed.
claim_boundary.next_test: Decide which numeral or alphabet re-presentations ARE structure-preserving: classify the monoid homomorphisms between free monoids on different alphabet sizes that are injective (codes) or onto (decoders), and prove which of them preserve atoms, as the next step beyond the isomorphism obstruction proved here.
